approach:
Add one reading check, `check_part_coverage(reading, request)`, as one new `step!(check_part_coverage(reading, request));` line placed last in `refusing_check`. A new parser `request_parts` in topics.rs reads numbered parts `(N)`, `N.`, `N)` (runs 1,2,3.. of at least two) and the dash or star bullets of the Acceptance section (all bullets when no opener exists). `is_bullet` and `request_text_acceptance` stay untouched. Quoted or backticked spans, fenced blocks, `>` lines, generated lines and everything after `## Source` are never read as markers. A length-preserving mask finds the markers, and the item text is cut from the original line with the quote characters stripped. Guard: `reading.capability.is_none() || reading.question.is_some()` returns Ok (same as checks.rs:415).

COVERAGE. An item is covered by any one of three routes.
(i) MARKER CITATION: a criterion that names the part's marker (`(3)`, `part 3`, `item 3`, digit-bounded) covers that part, unless that criterion itself has a deferral phrase. The refusal message teaches starting a criterion with the marker.
(ii) REGRESSION BULLET: an item with a test-pass phrase (`tests? (still |now )?pass(es)?`) whose other own stems all lie in REGRESSION_STEMS {unrel, behav, other, regre, break} is covered by any criterion with a test-pass phrase or `cargo test`. This is the Steward bullet 'No unrelated behavior changes; the existing tests pass' (steward.rs:621-623), so a reading whose criterion says only 'cargo test passes' is not refused (finding 4). 'fmt, clippy and test pass' has the stem `clipp`, so it is not a regression bullet and `cargo test` alone does not cover it.
(iii) STEM FALLBACK: the item's own distinctive stems (stems found in a sibling item removed; all stems when none remain) must share min(2, ceil(n/2)) stems with one criterion. Items with no stem are unchecked. Reading text is tokenised whole with quoted spans kept.

DEFERRAL. It is searched in summary, assumptions, departures and out_of_scope, never in criteria. Clauses are cut on `;` and on a comma only when the next words start a marker or part word (`, part 3`, `, (3)`, `, and (3)`). So 'Part (3), which was the slowest, is left for a follow-up job' stays one clause. A clause defers an item when it has a deferral phrase (follow-up, deferred, later job, separate job, not in this job, left for), no negation guard (never, without, refus, unless, do not, not defer), and names the item by marker or by own-stem overlap. Past guard (finding 6): in summary, assumptions and departures a clause is skipped only when a past word (was, were, had been, been, already, previously) sits within the 3 words immediately before the deferral phrase, or the clause has `(earlier|previous|prior|last) (reading|attempt|job|result|run|plan)`, or it names a job id. An incidental 'was' elsewhere in the clause does not skip it. An out_of_scope item counts only with a deferral phrase naming it, or when it is the whole part (bare marker, or it restates the part's stems and adds none).

SPLIT EXEMPTION. Per clause (cut on `;` and `,`) it needs a modal, no negation, no complaint word, and Shape A (move verb, at most 4 object words with no path-like token, preposition, determiner `a`/`an`/none, then a split-signal adjective before job/change/PR/request, or a plural noun with several/multiple) or Shape B (marker or part word as subject of be/become, `a`/`an`/none, follow-up/separate/later/another, job/change/PR). A clause naming markers exempts only those parts; one naming none exempts every item.

FIXTURES (findings 1-3). `crates/athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs` is NOT edited. The Scenario verdict is `passing_verdict(2)` (common/mod.rs:500) and verify.rs:533-543 matches verdict entries to reading criteria by index, with an unmatched criterion recorded `met: false`. So adding criteria to the Scenario reader would break the CLI tests (the critic's finding 2). Instead: (a) `fake.rs` `reader_turn` adds one content criterion per request bullet or numbered line. That is safe because the fake producer and verifier build their criteria and verdict from the brief's criteria list (fake.rs:328-338, 389-395), so they stay index-matched. (b) For the CLI tests, the producer runs `cargo test --locked` first and fixes only the tests actually refused. The one known case is job_plan.rs:166/169, whose bullet 'the demo study has a pin' is not covered by the default reading. Its bullet becomes 'README.md ends with a greeting line', the text of the default reading's own criterion (common/mod.rs:364), so criteria count and verdict size are unchanged. The `rated_scenario` tests (drain.rs:3988, 4067, 4069, 4492, 6056-6085) already have the criterion 'the demo study has a pin, claims and an intro' and are unaffected. Any other refused test is fixed the same way: change its bullet to a covered text, or set `scenario.reading` and `scenario.verdict = passing_verdict(n)` with n the reading's criteria count. Never loosen the check.

The reader brief gets no rule (briefs.rs and briefs/reader.rs unchanged). The refusal message carries the repair.

decisions.choice: Coverage has three routes: marker citation, regression-bullet route, then own-stem overlap min(2, ceil(n/2)) with sibling-shared stems removed and a fall-back to all stems.
decisions.reason: A part whose only own stem is a weak verb would otherwise refuse natural criteria; citing the marker is a sure repair. The Steward bullet 'No unrelated behavior changes; the existing tests pass' has own stems {unrel, behav} after the stop list, so a reading whose criterion says only 'cargo test passes' or 'the tests still pass' would be refused without route (ii) (finding 4). Restricting route (ii) to items whose other stems are all in REGRESSION_STEMS keeps 'fmt, clippy and test pass' needing a clippy criterion.

rejected.option: Let any `cargo test` criterion cover any item containing 'test pass'
rejected.why: The Steward bullet 'fmt, clippy and test pass' would be covered by cargo test alone, and the dropped-clippy twin would be accepted.

decisions.choice: Distinctive stem order is fixed and written in a code comment: lowercase token; drop trailing s if longer than 4; reject under 4 chars; reject if the raw or singular word is in the stop list (checked BEFORE the cut); cut to 5. The stop list holds domain words (test, tests, pass, passes, change, changes, described, existing, job, part, request, fmt, made, make) and English function words of 4+ letters (with, that, from, each, when, into, only, this, then, than, they, them, have, will, would, should, which, there, their, these, those, also, such, some, same, more, most, must, does, been, being, both, over, under, once, after, before, about, other, used, uses, using, need, needs, where, what), listed in the comment. REGRESSION_STEMS is a second const next to it. A unit test pins 'with','that','from','changes','described','existing','tests','pass' as not distinctive, 'clippy' and 'cover' as distinctive, 'default' = 'defaults'.
decisions.reason: Stop words are full words, so the stop check must run before the cut; function words would otherwise become own stems.

rejected.why: Full-word entries never match cut stems.
